issues.description: The template's Stock.findStockIngredient method signature does not match the problem UML and how it's used elsewhere in the template. The problem specification and example usage expect findStockIngredient(String), but the template declares findStockIngredient(String, boolean). Additionally, other methods in the same template (add, take) call findStockIngredient with a single String parameter, which makes the template self-contradictory and causes compilation errors for students attempting to call findStockIngredient(String).
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template Stock class to provide a findStockIngredient(String name) method (matching the UML and example usage), or add an overloaded findStockIngredient(String) that delegates to the existing method. Ensure the method signature in the template matches the problem statement and the example calls (single String parameter).

issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to initialize the stock attribute in the SealSaloon constructor, but also explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static (shared across instances) and final. Initializing a static final field in an instance constructor contradicts the static requirement and is not appropriate Java practice. This creates confusion about whether stock should be instance-initialized in the constructor or declared static and initialized at declaration or in a static initializer.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the instructions: state that the stock field is static and should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer (not in the instance constructor). Update the problem text to remove the instruction to initialize the shared stock in the instance constructor and instead instruct students to initialize orders in the constructor and the shared stock at declaration (or in a static block).

issues.description: The problem statement and the solution expect Stock.findStockIngredient(String) (single String parameter) but the template repository's Stock class defines findStockIngredient(String, boolean). This signature mismatch (extra boolean parameter controlling case-sensitivity) creates a direct API/name mapping inconsistency: students reading the problem and tests will look for a one-argument method while the provided template uses a different method signature, causing confusion and potential compilation/test failures.
issues.suggestedFix: Adjust the template Stock class to provide the same API as described in the problem and implemented in the solution: add or rename to public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) (single parameter). If case-sensitivity control is desired, provide an internal overload or a separate method, but ensure the one-argument signature exists to match the problem statement and tests.
